warning: Prototype conversation support only. Not mediation, legal advice, safety planning, therapy, emergency support, ritual instruction, or spiritual authority.

situations.signal: You need to respond, but the first reply may be sharper than the real need.
situations.draft: I want to answer carefully, not react quickly. Give me a little time and I will come back with a clearer response.
situations.reflection: Can this reply be truthful, useful, and less agitating?
situations.boundary: Reflection support only. Not mediation, legal advice, safety planning, therapy, or spiritual authority.

situations.signal: Something true needs to be said without turning truth into a weapon.
situations.draft: I want to be honest and respectful. Here is what I am seeing, and I am open to hearing what I may be missing.
situations.reflection: Is the message true, timely, and useful, or only emotionally satisfying?
situations.boundary: Not a command to speak in every situation. Safety and context matter.

situations.signal: You see your part and want to repair without performing guilt.
situations.draft: I am sorry for my part in this. I can see how it affected you. I will be more careful with this specific action next time.
situations.reflection: What part is mine to own clearly, without explaining it away?
situations.boundary: Not legal advice, confession handling, clinical repair, or pressure for forgiveness.

situations.signal: You need to say no without becoming cold or overexplaining.
situations.draft: I cannot take this on right now. I respect the need, but I need to keep my boundary clear.
situations.reflection: Can the no be clear, kind, and free from unnecessary defense?
situations.boundary: Not safety planning, legal advice, workplace HR guidance, or family mediation.

situations.signal: Care, expectation, and old patterns are mixed together.
situations.draft: I care about this relationship, and I want to speak with respect. I can help with one concrete thing, but I cannot carry the whole situation.
situations.reflection: What is respectful care, and what is control wearing the language of care?
situations.boundary: Not family therapy, medical advice, elder-care instruction, legal advice, or a rule for every household.

situations.signal: Work pressure is making the message either defensive or vague.
situations.draft: Here is what I can own, here is the next step, and here is what I need from the team to move cleanly.
situations.reflection: Which part of this work is mine to do, and which part needs a clear request?
situations.boundary: Not employment advice, HR guidance, legal advice, or a promise of success.

situations.signal: You want to thank someone without making it dramatic or transactional.
situations.draft: Thank you for what you did. It mattered to me because it made this specific part of life easier.
situations.reflection: Can gratitude name the concrete gift without demanding anything back?
situations.boundary: Not ritual instruction, social scripting for every culture, or emotional obligation.

situations.signal: The mind keeps replaying the conversation and needs a clean next step.
situations.draft: I have thought about our conversation. One thing I want to repair is this: I should have listened before responding.
situations.reflection: What one repair action can I take without trying to control the outcome?
situations.boundary: Not mediation, safety planning, therapy, legal advice, or pressure to reconnect.
